name: Alpheus Alphaeus
overview: The Scriptures identify Alphaeus (also spelled Alpheus) primarily as the father of two of Jesus' disciples, James and Levi. James is mentioned as the son of Alphaeus in both Matthew 10:3 and Mark 3:18, highlighting his role among the twelve apostles. Similarly, Levi, who is also called Matthew the publican, is described as the son of Alphaeus in Mark 2:14, where Jesus calls him to follow Him while he is at the tax collector's booth. These references emphasize Alphaeus' familial connection to key followers of Christ who responded to His call to discipleship.
